brand.title: ESourceAIG (Production)
brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource WhiteLabel Sales Course

questions.question: What are the three main reasons firms buy the white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Their brand, data stays home, and lower cost per client
Bank feeds, payroll integration, and mobile app access
Client login portal, live feeds, and unlimited support
QuickBooks compatibility, Xero integration, and Wave support
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these three reasons are the core value proposition and should be deliverable in one breath during a sales conversation.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While some of these features exist in competitors' tools, the three core reasons firms buy this white-label solution are their brand visibility, data privacy (stays home), and cost savings per client.

questions.question: According to the course, what is the ideal firm size to target for this white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Enterprise accounting firms with 500+ monthly clients
Bookkeeping and small CPA firms with roughly 5 to 100 monthly clients
Solo practitioners with fewer than 5 monthly clients
Nationwide accounting networks with multiple office locations
questions.feedback_correct: You've identified the sweet spot—firms in this range have enough clients to benefit from pricing tiers but still value brand control and data privacy.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course specifically defines the best fit as bookkeeping and small CPA firms with approximately 5 to 100 monthly clients; firms outside this range may have different needs or not yet be a good fit for this tool.

questions.question: How should you calculate pricing for a prospect with 38 client books?
choices: Multiply 38 by $15 and divide by 12 months
Call Joe to confirm the exact pricing before quoting anything
Open the price calculator at app.esourcebookkeeper.com/calculator and enter 38
Use the Competitor Battle Cards document to reference the nearest competitor's rate
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—the calculator handles the tiered math automatically and shows the monthly bill, average per book, and yearly total without error.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Never do pricing math by hand; the calculator tool ensures accuracy across tiered bands and saves time during the sales conversation.

questions.question: What should you emphasize in the demo if a prospect mentions they spend a lot of time chasing clients about unsorted transactions?
choices: The Health dashboard colors and P and L report features
The firm-branded logo screen at the beginning of the demo
The reminders feature—showing how texts and calendar reminders chase clients automatically
The AI Suggest categories feature and how it automates sorting
questions.feedback_correct: Great instinct—the reminders demo moment directly solves the pain point by showing how bookkeepers can text or email clients about missing statements from their own phone.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While other features are valuable, the reminders moment (Status tab with red flags, Text client functionality, and calendar reminders) is specifically designed to land with bookkeepers frustrated by manual chasing.

questions.question: What discovery question should you ask to uncover a prospect's feelings about competitor price increases?
choices: Which software are your clients on, and who pays for it?
How did this year's price increases hit you and your clients?
Whose name do your clients see when they get their reports?
How many hours a month go to chasing clients about transactions?
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—this cost-focused question opens the door to discussing QuickBooks' August 2026 increase and other pain points that make your pricing competitive.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The discovery questions are designed to uncover specific pain: tools used, cost frustrations, brand visibility, and time spent on transaction management. The price increase question targets the cost category.

questions.question: How do you respond to the objection "Our clients already know QuickBooks"?
choices: Explain that QuickBooks has better bank feeds than the white-label tool
Agree that switching is difficult and suggest waiting a year before trying
Point out that clients get Excel reports with your firm's name and don't need to learn any software
Recommend that clients stick with QuickBooks for familiarity and only use the white-label tool internally
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—clients don't interact with the software itself; they receive branded reports with the firm's name, so their familiarity with QuickBooks is irrelevant.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Clients never need to log into or learn the white-label tool; they receive Excel reports branded with your firm's name, so existing software knowledge is not a barrier.

questions.question: What makes the firm's data security story compelling enough to overcome concerns about employee departures?
choices: ESource stores all backups on secure cloud servers with military-grade encryption
Only added users can sign in with their own email, and when removed, books lock at next check-in even on personal laptops; backups are locked to the firm too
The tool requires two-factor authentication and monthly password changes for all staff
A third-party security audit is conducted every quarter to verify data integrity
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—you've captured the core security story: access control, automatic locking, and backup protection that ensures clients stay with the firm even if an employee leaves.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The security story hinges on access control (owner adds users), automatic locking (books lock when a user is removed), and backup protection (backups locked to firm); this addresses the owner's core fear: losing clients to a departing employee.

questions.question: Why is it important to propose a 3- to 5-client pilot for 60 days rather than asking the prospect to switch all clients at once?
choices: A pilot allows ESource to test the firm's data quality before full implementation
The pilot reduces risk by running alongside their current system, allows success measures to be tested, and builds confidence before full migration
Pilots are required by law before any accounting software can be fully deployed
A pilot lets you charge a lower rate and upsell them on the full version later
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—the pilot strategy removes perceived risk, creates measurable wins (hours saved, fewer questions, better reports), and sets up a natural path to full migration.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pilot is a risk-reduction strategy that allows the prospect to validate success before committing all clients; it's not a compliance requirement or pricing tactic, but rather a closing technique that builds confidence.

questions.question: How should you handle the objection "We need bank feeds" when a prospect raises it?
choices: Apologize and explain that bank feeds will be added in the next software update
Agree to contact Joe about custom integration options for their specific bank
Explain that monthly downloads take minutes, every month is proven to tie to the bank, and many firms prefer this to feeds that silently miss transactions
Suggest they keep QuickBooks Online for feeds and use the white-label tool only for reporting
questions.feedback_correct: Spot-on—you've reframed the perceived weakness (no automatic feeds) into a potential strength (verified reconciliation every month with no silent misses).
questions.feedback_incorrect: The objection about bank feeds is addressed by showing that monthly downloads are quick, the tie to the bank is proven each month, and many firms actually prefer this method because automatic feeds can miss transactions silently.

questions.question: When presenting the tool's unique features to differentiate from competitors, which feature should you mention first because no competitor has a direct equivalent?
choices: The Health dashboard with color-coded alerts and P and L reports
A spoken help assistant inside the product that staff can ask questions to out loud or via text
The ability to download Excel reports branded with the firm's name
AI-powered category suggestions and draft client questions
questions.feedback_correct: Excellent—the spoken help assistant is a unique differentiator; none of the checked competitors offer this feature, and it directly reduces support calls for the firm.
questions.feedback_incorrect: While other features are valuable, the course specifically highlights that the spoken help assistant—where staff can ask out loud or type and get step-by-step answers—is a competitive advantage that competitors don't match.
